solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Justification OK for uprising (11)

blocks.note: grounds = justification, as in 'grounds for complaint'
well = OK, as in 'all is well'

explanation.surface: Someone is looking for a reason that would make a revolt acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'OK' as approval of the uprising; in fact it is just a second chunk of letters placed after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundswell is a rising surge of feeling or support, a popular uprising.

clue.text: Pick up sheep that’s rolled over (3)

indicators.note: something rolled over is turned upside down, so in a down clue the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: A farmer lifts a sheep that has toppled onto its back.
explanation.walkthrough: TEG is a crossword regular: a two-year-old sheep. Pick up means get, as in picking up or getting a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up something, such as an idea or an illness, is to get it.

clue.text: Leather releasing hydrogen compound (5)

indicators.note: the leather lets go of the hydrogen, which drops out

blocks.note: oxhide is leather made from an ox's skin
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen; it is removed

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about leather giving off a hydrogen compound.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'hydrogen compound' as one chemical phrase; they split, with hydrogen feeding the wordplay and compound alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with another element.

clue.text: Edible strands rarely working when 1000 cut up (7)

indicators.note: the thousand is cut away from the letters
in a down clue, up means the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: seldom = rarely
on = working, as a machine is on
M is the Roman numeral for 1000; removing it leaves SELDOON

explanation.surface: A cook notes that noodles rarely work once a thousand are chopped up.
explanation.walkthrough: SELDOM + ON loses its M to leave SELDOON, which read upwards is NOODLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are long thin strands of pasta or dough that are eaten.

clue.text: Top sandwich in America (6,3)

blocks.note: a top is a garment for the upper body; here a loose, baggy sweater
an American bun filled with minced beef in a tomato sauce

explanation.surface: A food critic names the best sandwich in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like praise for the sandwich; it is a garment, a sweater, which is the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy joe names both a baggy jumper (sweater) and a messy minced-beef sandwich popular in the US.

clue.text: Fluff stuck inside upright freezer or refrigerator (5)

indicators.note: the answer is lodged within the following words
in a down clue, standing upright means the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: freezeR OR REfrigerator

explanation.surface: Some dust has got stuck inside an upright fridge-freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright freezer' looks like a type of appliance; 'upright' in fact tells you to read the hidden letters upwards. To fluff is to make a mistake, so a fluff is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluff is a blunder, such as a fluffed line or shot, which is an error.

clue.text: Italian food, while in wrap, irrelevant (7)

indicators.note: 'while in wrap' puts the word for while physically in the word for wrap, so AS sits inside LAG

blocks.note: as = while, as in 'as I was leaving'
to lag is to wrap pipes or a tank in insulation
NA = not applicable, written on forms where a question is irrelevant

explanation.surface: Someone declares Italian food irrelevant while eating a wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pipes are lagged, wrapped against frost. The 'wrap' looks like a rival food; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is the Italian baked dish of flat pasta sheets layered with sauce.

clue.text: What’s unknown on heads in France and England? (3)

definitions.text: What’s unknown on heads in France and England?

indicators.note: the heads of France and England are their first letters

blocks.note: the first letters of France and England
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A quiz asks what hat is never seen on French or English heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a fez is a hat you would not see on heads in France or England, and its letters are F, E and an unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: A fez is a brimless red hat rarely worn in France or England, so it is unknown on heads there.

clue.text: Free pay, easy! (9)

blocks.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
loose = easy, relaxed, as in 'hang loose'

explanation.surface: An advert promises money for nothing: free pay, easy!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free pay' reads as one phrase; free is the definition and pay the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Footloose means free to go where one likes, without ties.

clue.text: Fly: fly quicker shielding wings on extension (3,8)

indicators.note: FASTER covers and protects EN inside it
the wings of a word are its two outer letters

blocks.note: to zip = to fly along
faster = quicker
the outer letters of 'extension'

explanation.surface: An insect: a fly that goes faster with its wings on an extension.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Fly' is the trouser fly, fastened with a zip; the second is the verb, to zip along.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly on trousers is the opening closed by a zip fastener.

clue.text: Fabric missing hem, lower flag (9)

indicators.note: a hem is an edge, so the fabric loses its final letter

blocks.note: tricot is a knitted fabric; without its last letter it is TRICO
to lower or lour is to frown or look threatening, rhyming with 'flower'

explanation.surface: A tailor, fabric unfinished, is told to lower a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not the opposite of raise but the verb meaning to scowl, also spelt LOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricolour is a flag of three colour bands, such as the French flag.

clue.text: Block surrounding opening to exterior part of Cape Town property (5)

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it on all sides, so STOP is split to hold the E
the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to stop = to block
first letter of 'exterior'

explanation.surface: Blocks around the entrance to a building's outside in Cape Town.
explanation.walkthrough: STOEP is a South African word from Afrikaans, known to crossword solvers more than most.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoep is the raised veranda at the front of a South African house.

clue.text: Accessory in relationship cut (3,4)

blocks.note: a tie = a bond or relationship, as in family ties
to clip = to cut

explanation.surface: A fashion accessory features in a couple's break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relationship cut' reads as a break-up; the two words each give a chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie clip is a small accessory holding a necktie to the shirt.

clue.text: Whale, spirit heard in powerful music (6,5)

indicators.note: we hear the word rather than read it, so METTLE is spelt METAL

blocks.note: to whale is to beat or thrash
mettle = spirit, courage

explanation.surface: A whale's spirit can be heard in stirring music, perhaps a whale song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whale' is not the animal but the old verb meaning to beat hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrash metal is a fast, aggressive, loud style of heavy metal music.

clue.text: Fancy gear associated with leaders in administration primarily? (7)

definitions.text: Fancy gear associated with leaders in administration primarily?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb, to imagine, so the letters of gear are reimagined
the first letters of the words before it

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
first letters of leaders, in and administration

explanation.surface: Ceremonial dress is linked above all to those running a government.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: regalia is the fancy gear worn by people who lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the ceremonial robes and emblems of office worn by rulers and officials.

clue.text: Return setter’s first exceptional puzzle (5)

indicators.note: the letters come back the other way
only the first letter of setter's

blocks.note: first letter of 'setter's'
uber = exceptional, super

explanation.surface: A plea to give back the setter's first-rate puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptional' looks like praise for the puzzle; it gives UBER, the borrowed German word for super.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures or symbols stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Complains tree is cut (9)

blocks.note: to beef = to complain
teak is a hardwood tree

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a tree has been felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree is cut' looks like a statement about felling; 'cut' is a noun, a cut of meat, and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefsteak is a thick slice cut from beef.

clue.text: Sauce label off, pretty much (4,5)

blocks.note: jus is a thin meat gravy
a tab is a label or tag
off = out, as when the lights are off

explanation.surface: The label on a sauce bottle has nearly come off.
explanation.walkthrough: The chunks ignore the word break in the answer: the sauce and label run straight across it, so do not look for a four-letter sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Just about means almost or nearly, the same as pretty much.

clue.text: Wind blast, absurd (9)

blocks.note: to screw is to wind or twist
a blast = a ball, a great time, as in 'we had a ball'

explanation.surface: A weather report: a gust of wind, and a ridiculous one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind blast' looks like a gale; wind rhymes with 'find' here and blast means a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwball, as an adjective, means crazy or absurd.

clue.text: Get upset with partner wearing fleece (4,1,4)

indicators.note: DATE is dressed in SHEAR, sitting inside it

blocks.note: a date = a romantic partner
to fleece a sheep is to shear it

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that their partner has turned up in a fleece jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like a garment for the partner to wear; it is the verb, to shear.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: shedding a tear is the outward sign of being upset, so the phrase stands for getting upset.

clue.text: Player with cavil originally splitting a hair (7)

indicators.note: the original, first letter of cavil
C splits TRESS by going into it

blocks.note: A as printed
first letter of 'cavil'
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: An actor with a quibble at first is splitting hairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'splitting hairs', to cavil; here the C goes in after the A, ahead of TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Player is an old word for anyone acting on stage, as in Hamlet's 'the players', so a female actor qualifies.

clue.text: Honest family takes up crime in the end (5)

indicators.note: CLAN takes in the E, holding it
only the last letter of crime

blocks.note: a clan is a family group
last letter of 'crime'

explanation.surface: A law-abiding family finally turns to crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a family going bad; 'takes up' means only that CLAN encloses a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean means honest, free of wrongdoing, as in a clean record.

clue.text: Jersey etc wrapped round new hat in red (7)

indicators.note: CI wraps round the anagram
the letters of hat in are made new, rearranged

blocks.note: CI = the Channel Islands, of which Jersey is one
anagram fodder, 5 letters

explanation.surface: A jersey and other clothes are wrapped round a new red hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like a sweater; it is the island. 'In red' reads as a colour, but 'red' alone is the definition, a red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: 'red' is short for red wine, and this Tuscan wine is one of the best known.

clue.text: Darling rejected by girl — gaffe! (7)

indicators.note: rejected, sent back, so PET reads backwards

blocks.note: a miss is a girl
pet = darling, as a term of endearment

explanation.surface: Someone calls a girl 'darling' and she rebuffs it: a social blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By girl' does the ordering: the rejected darling ends up after the girl, even though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstep is a wrong move or mistake, a gaffe.

clue.text: Ill-feeling cut short card game (5)

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: piquet, an old card game for two; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A card game ended early, leaving bad feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Piquet is an old two-player card game, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is resentment or irritation from wounded pride, an ill-feeling.

clue.text: Hair in mixer? (7)

blocks.note: a single hair, especially one on the face or a cat's muzzle
a whisk mixes, so a playful name for a mixer is one that whisks

explanation.surface: A cook finds a stray hair in the food mixer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented second sense: add -ER to whisk and you get a thing that whisks, a mixer.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisker is a plain synonym for a hair, and read as whisk + -er it jokingly names a kitchen mixer.

clue.text: Mould close to moisture in rising damp (5)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter
the moisture's last letter is literally in the damp, placed inside its word
in a down clue, rising means reading bottom to top

blocks.note: last letter of 'moisture'
dank = damp

explanation.surface: Mould forms near moisture where there is rising damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mould' is the fungus in the surface; the definition is the verb, to shape by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead dough is to mould it by pressing and folding with the hands.

clue.text: Idea in force, briefly (5)

indicators.note: the phrase is cut short by a letter

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force; the phrase loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A concept that is in effect for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In force' reads as 'in effect'; 'in' is only a link, and 'force' is a police force, the Met.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a central idea, the subject of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Search patrols aren’t more odd, compared to others (9)

indicators.note: to patrol an area is to go all round it, so QUEST goes round AINT

blocks.note: a quest is a search
ain't = aren't, informally

explanation.surface: Search patrols declare they are not any odder than other patrols.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a roundabout superlative: more odd than all the others is the most odd, the quaintest.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaintest means oddest in a charming, old-fashioned way, odder than all others.

clue.text: Sea dog, animal sailing north (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading bottom to top

blocks.note: a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: An old sailor and a ship's animal sail north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea dog' looks like an animal, feeding the surface's animal theme; it is an old sailor, a tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tar, like a sea dog, is an old-fashioned word for a sailor.

clue.text: She abandons one currency before backing — another? (3)

indicators.note: she abandons the currency, walking out of it, so her three letters are removed from the word
what remains goes backwards

blocks.note: the shekel is the currency of Israel
SHE as printed, removed to leave KEL

explanation.surface: A woman gives up one currency before switching to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another?' points back to 'currency': the answer is a second currency. The lek is the currency of Albania.
explanation.definitionFit: The lek, Albania's currency, is another currency after the shekel.

clue.text: Signal file fascinating political speaker? (11)

blocks.note: to spell = to signal, as in 'this spells trouble'
a binder is a file for papers

explanation.surface: A document signals that a politician's speech was riveting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a spellbinder is any compelling speaker, especially a politician who holds a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A spellbinder is an orator who holds an audience spellbound, often a politician.
